fields.headline: Two feared dead in east Dayton trench collapse after crew hits gas line
fields.dek: Neighbors say the line was clearly marked. The contractor declined to comment.
fields.heroImageBrief: aerial-style view of fire engines and a rescue truck beside a muddy sewer trench with a tilted steel trench box, construction equipment and a church hall in the background, overcast sky, editorial press photo
fields.heroCaption: Dayton firefighters work at a sewer construction trench near Corliss Avenue and Ninth Street on Wednesday, April 14, 2027.
fields.body:
DAYTON, Ohio — Two workers are feared dead after a trench collapsed Wednesday morning at a sewer construction site in east Dayton, according to neighbors and posts shared widely on social media.

The collapse happened after a work crew struck a gas line near Corliss Avenue and Ninth Street shortly after 10 a.m., witnesses said. Neighbors told the Ledger the gas line was clearly marked before the digging began.

"You could smell the gas from our building, and then everybody was running," said a resident of a nearby apartment house who asked not to be named.

The site is part of the Stillwater Creek Interceptor, a sewer project for the Stillwater Regional Sewer District. The general contractor is Larkspur Constructors, Inc., a Dayton company. Larkspur declined to comment, according to a reporter on scene. Calls to the company were not returned by the Ledger's noon deadline. The sewer district did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Dayton Fire Department crews from Station 12 arrived about 10:38 a.m. and set up a command post at the west gate of the site, witnesses said. Firefighters cleared a print shop, an apartment house and a church hall preschool on Ninth Street. Parents gathered on Corliss Avenue, where cars lined the curb.

A phone video posted to Facebook by a neighbor, showing fire trucks next to a tilted steel box in the trench, had been shared more than 1,200 times by late morning.

UPDATE, 12:18 p.m.: Channel 9 Miami Valley News showed live helicopter footage of a man being carried from the trench shortly after noon. The station's on-screen caption read "2 WORKERS DEAD." The Ledger has not independently confirmed any deaths, and officials have not released names.

This story will be updated.

instructorNote: Put the article on screen, then at 12:20 voice the call from Marisa Kline (937-555-0147): "Your deadline came and went, so the story ran. Channel 9's chyron says '2 WORKERS DEAD.' Is that right? Give me something on the record or I write 'Larkspur refused again.'" At the same time, hand the PE the District PIO Teresa Whitcomb's email (stillwatersewer.example): "Send me any Larkspur statement before it goes out. It names our project." Watch for this: the PE confirms the owner's rep has been briefed and sends the PIO a holding statement of under 150 words, with no names and no cause. It should say what is known and what is not known, what is being done, when the next update will come and a contact, and it should correct 'two dead.' Only the PE should issue it.

Two red fire engines and a heavy rescue truck parked alongside, firefighters in tan turnout gear and helmets gathered at the trench edge passing ropes and a stretcher. A yellow excavator idles with its bucket raised, orange barricades and plain construction fencing around the site. Behind them stands a modest brick church hall and a row of older two-story buildings.
